source_page_convention: source_page is the printed curriculum page; pdf_page is the PDF page number

indicator.subject: Religious and Moral Education
indicator.content_standard: BI. 1.1.1. Explain who the Creator is

skills.description: Recognise the examples and vocabulary in the lesson.
Explain meanings and connections in an example.

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.
misconceptions: A human provider is confused with the Creator
A possession is confused with a basic need
Providing a need is confused with originating all things
spec.teacherGuidance: Read questions aloud when needed. Assess understanding of the curriculum teaching, not the child's personal belief. Accept clear oral responses in a familiar language.

questions.stem: In our RME lesson, who is the Creator?
hints: Think about who the lesson says began all things.
questions.explanation: The lesson calls God the originator of all things. This means God is the Creator.
questions.misconception: A human provider is confused with the Creator

distractor_misconceptions.A teacher: A teacher's help is confused with creation
distractor_misconceptions.A farmer: A farmer's work is confused with creation
distractor_misconceptions.A driver: A driver's work is confused with creation

questions.stem: Which word means the one who began all things?
hints: Think about the word used for God in this lesson.
questions.explanation: An originator begins something. Our lesson uses Creator for God, the originator of all things.
questions.misconception: Providing a need is confused with originating all things

distractor_misconceptions.Neighbour: Living nearby is confused with originating

questions.stem: Complete this lesson sentence: God is the ___ of all things.
hints: Use a word that means the one who began something.
questions.explanation: The lesson says God originated all things. Creator or originator completes the sentence.
questions.misconception: Providing a need is confused with originating all things

questions.stem: Which need do we use when we breathe?
hints: Think about what goes in and out as you breathe.
questions.explanation: We breathe air. Air is one of the needs the curriculum says God provides.
questions.misconception: A possession is confused with a basic need

distractor_misconceptions.A bag: A carried possession is mistaken for breathing air
distractor_misconceptions.A toy: A plaything is mistaken for a basic need
distractor_misconceptions.A book: A learning item is mistaken for breathing air

questions.stem: Which need do we drink?
hints: Think about what is in a cup when you are thirsty.
questions.explanation: We drink water. Water is a need listed in the lesson about God's provision.
questions.misconception: A possession is confused with a basic need

distractor_misconceptions.A pencil: A writing item is mistaken for a drink
distractor_misconceptions.A chair: Furniture is mistaken for a drink
distractor_misconceptions.A ball: A plaything is mistaken for a drink

questions.stem: Tell a partner what our lesson means when it calls God the Creator.
hints: Think about the beginning of all things.
questions.explanation: Explain the word Creator first. Then connect it to the teaching that God originated all things.

criteria.description: Explains creating or originating as beginning or bringing things into existence.
Links that meaning to God in the curriculum teaching.

questions.stem: Your friend asks, 'Why does our lesson call God the originator?' Give a short reply.
hints: Think about what the word originator tells us.
questions.explanation: Start with the meaning of originator. Explain how it describes God's role in the lesson.

criteria.description: Relates originator to the beginning of things.
States that the lesson teaches God originated all things.

questions.stem: Ama feels thirsty after play. Which listed need will help her?
hints: Choose something she can drink.
questions.explanation: Ama is thirsty, so she needs a drink. Water meets that need and is listed in the lesson.
questions.misconception: A possession is confused with a basic need

distractor_misconceptions.A ribbon: Decoration is mistaken for meeting thirst
distractor_misconceptions.A whistle: A sound-making item is mistaken for meeting thirst
distractor_misconceptions.A marble: A toy is mistaken for meeting thirst

questions.stem: Kojo is hungry at home. Which listed need should he receive?
hints: Think about what we eat.
questions.explanation: Kojo needs something to eat. Food meets hunger and is a need named in the lesson.
questions.misconception: A possession is confused with a basic need

distractor_misconceptions.A badge: A badge is confused with nourishment
distractor_misconceptions.A kite: A toy is confused with nourishment
distractor_misconceptions.A bell: A bell is confused with nourishment

questions.stem: The lesson names air, food, water and one more gift. What is that gift?
hints: Think about being alive.
questions.explanation: Recall the four examples in the lesson. Along with air, food and water, it names life.
questions.misconception: A possession is confused with a basic need

questions.stem: Name two needs in our lesson and tell when you use each one.
hints: Think about eating, drinking or breathing.
questions.explanation: Choose two needs from the lesson. Connect each to an everyday use.

criteria.description: Names two listed needs: air, food, water or life.
Gives a sensible everyday connection for each chosen need.

questions.stem: Tell one way today's breakfast connects with our lesson about God providing needs.
hints: Think about which need breakfast meets.
questions.explanation: Identify the need met by breakfast. Then link it to the curriculum teaching about God as provider.

criteria.description: Identifies breakfast as food meeting hunger.
Connects food with the lesson's teaching about God providing needs.

questions.stem: Esi eats lunch and drinks water. Name the two needs she uses. Explain how both connect to our lesson.
hints: Take the eating and drinking parts one at a time.
questions.explanation: Identify each need from the action. Relate both to the teaching that God provides our needs.

criteria.description: Identifies food and water.
Connects both to the curriculum teaching about provision.

questions.stem: Kofi says, 'My parent gives me food, so my parent is the Creator of all things.' Explain what he has mixed up.
hints: Compare helping someone with beginning all things.
questions.explanation: Recognise the parent's help. Then distinguish that help from the curriculum's meaning of Creator.

criteria.description: Acknowledges that parents can provide meals.
Distinguishes providing a meal from originating all things.
Identifies God as Creator within the lesson.

questions.stem: Draw yourself using one need from this lesson. Tell your teacher which need you drew and how the picture connects to the lesson.
hints: Choose an everyday action such as eating or drinking.
questions.explanation: Choose a listed need, show its use, and explain the connection. Assess meaning rather than drawing skill.

criteria.description: Depicts using a need listed in the lesson.
Names the depicted need.
Connects it to the lesson about God providing needs.

questions.stem: One child drinks water. Another breathes air. Explain how these different actions connect to the same RME teaching.
hints: Name each need before finding the shared idea.
questions.explanation: The actions use different needs. Explain the shared teaching about their provision.

criteria.description: Identifies water and air as the needs used.
Links both to the curriculum teaching that God provides needs.

questions.stem: Your partner says this lesson is only about food. Use two other examples to show that the lesson covers more.
hints: Recall the other needs named in the lesson.
questions.explanation: Recall examples besides food. Use them to explain that the teaching includes several needs.

criteria.description: Names two of air, water and life.
Explains that God's provision in the lesson includes more than food.

questions.stem: Prepare a short talk for a friend who missed class. Explain Creator, name two needs, and connect one need to your day.
hints: Plan your talk in three small parts.
questions.explanation: Define the lesson's key word, give examples, and show an everyday connection.

criteria.description: Explains Creator as originator of all things in the lesson.
Names two listed needs.
Gives a sensible everyday use of one named need.

questions.stem: Yaw says, 'Creator only means someone who brings me water.' Explain what is missing, then give a fuller meaning from our lesson.
hints: Compare one helpful action with the origin of all things.
questions.explanation: Identify the narrow meaning in Yaw's statement. Replace it with the lesson's fuller meaning of Creator.

criteria.description: Explains that bringing water is one act of providing help.
Explains that Creator refers to originating all things.
Relates that fuller meaning to God in the curriculum.

questions.stem: Tell a tiny story about a child using two needs during a school day. End by connecting the story to God as Creator and provider in our lesson.
hints: Choose two actions first. Then think of a closing sentence about the lesson.
questions.explanation: Connect two everyday actions to listed needs. End with the teaching about creation and provision.

criteria.description: Includes two sensible school-day actions using listed needs.
Names or clearly identifies both needs.
Links the story to God as Creator and provider within the curriculum teaching.

uncertain: The content-standard code uses BI as printed, while this indicator uses B1. No code has been silently normalised.
